summary: EASD 2026 in Milan (28 Sep–2 Oct) is driving almost all GLP-1 search demand this week. Three items were published in journals on 29–30 Sep. Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 (The Lancet) is the biggest wave: 1,152 adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes lost 12.7% / 19.1% / 20.8% on average at 80 weeks, vs 4.0% on placebo. Mainstream outlets (NBC, TIME, SciAm, Guardian, Ars) covered it overnight, so it is at peak. Our edge there is precise framing, plus a separate 'not approved yet, avoid research-peptide versions' safety explainer. The best early windows are: petrelintide ZUPREME-1 (Lancet D&E, presented 30 Sep; amylin, up to 10.7% vs 1.7% at 42 weeks, with GI tolerability comparable to placebo) and the Zepbound vs Wegovy HD indirect comparison (4.5 points more weight loss at 15 mg). Both are covered mostly by trade and finance press so far, with little creator coverage. Other early windows: the orforglipron (Foundayo) vs oral semaglutide indirect comparison, the semaglutide ~40% fewer asthma attacks finding (ERS, observational, vs sulfonylureas), and a practical 'how to throw away your GLP-1 pen safely' piece driven by NYC needle-stick news. The Nordic pancreatic cancer registry and the 'stopping GLP-1' veterans study keep accelerating across snapshots. The SELECT mediation story is fading (momentum down to 58), so use it only as a supporting hook. Caution items: the Novo real-world 'escalate vs switch' MACE claim (industry-framed, invites switching questions), anesthesia on GLP-1, NAION and creatine. Each needs strict framing or should be deprioritized. Titles should carry the stated number plus population and timeframe, per the playbook.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 in The Lancet: adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes lost 12.7%, 19.1% and 20.8% on average at 80 weeks (4, 9, 12 mg) vs 4.0% on placebo; A1C down up to 1.6 points from 7.7%
candidates.angle: The calm, precise explainer everyone else is skipping. What a 'triple agonist' (GIP + GLP-1 + glucagon) is, the exact population (1,152 adults with obesity AND type 2 diabetes), why people with diabetes usually lose less than people without it (so ~21% here is notable), and what's still unknown: approval timing, longer-term safety and side effects. Title formula: 'Retatrutide: ~21% average weight loss at 80 weeks in adults with type 2 diabetes (TRIUMPH-2)'. Investigational, not approved as of Sept 2026; talk to your doctor.

candidates.topic: Petrelintide (amylin analogue) ZUPREME-1 phase 2: up to 10.7% average weight loss at 42 weeks vs 1.7% placebo, with GI tolerability comparable to placebo (Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, EASD 30 Sep)

Explain the other fullness hormone your pancreas releases alongside insulin, why amylin drugs might feel gentler on the stomach, and where this fits next to GLP-1 medicines. Be clear it's phase 2 in 485 adults, now moving to phase 3, and not available. A positive 'what's coming' piece that fits the next-gen pillar.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide 15 mg vs semaglutide 7.2 mg ('Wegovy HD'): 4.5 percentage points more average weight loss in an indirect comparison of SURMOUNT-1 and STEP UP (adults with obesity, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Which works better?' is the #1 question, and this answers it honestly. Explain what an indirect treatment comparison is (two separate trials, statistically adjusted, not head-to-head), that it's company-sponsored, and that the higher semaglutide dose itself is new. The takeaway: both are among the most effective medicines studied, and the right one depends on your health, coverage and tolerability, so decide with your prescriber. Avoid any switching advice.
candidates.why_now: Lilly announced it at EASD on 29 Sep. It spread through finance and trade press (Yahoo, Benzinga, Investing, TradingView), and consumer explainers haven't caught up. 'Zepbound vs Wegovy' is a perennial high-volume search that just got a fresh hook.

evidence.signal: 15 mg: 4.5% more; 10 mg: 3.2% more; covariate-adjusted ITC of SURMOUNT-1 and STEP UP

candidates.topic: Why you can't get retatrutide yet, and why 'research peptide' versions are risky (unapproved counterfeits and FDA concern)
candidates.angle: A protective explainer riding the retatrutide wave. The medicine is investigational and not approved as of Sept 2026. Products sold online as 'retatrutide' aren't the trial drug, and regulators have raised concerns. What to do instead: ask your doctor about approved options and trials. We never name sellers, never discuss doses and never show sourcing.
candidates.why_now: The TRIUMPH-2 hype is sending people to search for how to get the drug right now. Korean health press and bworldonline are already flagging unapproved counterfeits. Trustworthy safety content that ranks for 'buy retatrutide' searches is a public service.

candidates.topic: How to throw away your GLP-1 pen safely: NYC sanitation needle-stick injuries hit 57 so far in 2026 (vs 51 in all of 2025), and officials suspect rising injectable GLP-1 use
candidates.angle: A practical, kind 'life on GLP-1' tip. Pen needles count as sharps. Use an FDA-cleared sharps container or a strong plastic bottle, label it, and never put it in recycling. Check your local rules. Positive framing: a 30-second habit that protects the people who collect your trash. Say officials 'suspect' the GLP-1 link rather than stating it.
